days.title: Day 1: Linear Algebra, MatMul & Autograd
days.subtitle: The Math Kernel — building the foundation of every neural network
days.label: LinAlg

tasks.text: Watch 3Blue1Brown: Essence of Linear Algebra (Ch. 1–7). Focus on matrices as linear transformations, dot products as similarity, matmul as composing transformations.
Watch 3B1B Neural Networks Ch. 1–4 (~65 min): What is a neural network, Gradient descent, Backpropagation, Backprop calculus.
Watch Karpathy's 'The spelled-out intro to neural networks and backpropagation: building micrograd' (2.5 hrs). Code the 100-line Python autograd engine alongside him.
Solve Problem Set — Day 1: Cosine similarity by hand, Shape Inspector (matmul dimensions), Chain Rule trace.
Read The Personal MBA frameworks: 'Iron Law of the Market' and '12 Standard Forms of Value'.
Watch Y Combinator's 'How to Build a Product' (Michael Seibel). Understand why people part with money: reducing friction, saving time, mitigating risk, increasing status.
IEEE 754 Formats (FP32 vs FP16 vs BF16 vs FP8): Understand bit-level layout of Sign, Exponent, Mantissa. Why BF16 replaced FP16.
Einstein Summation (torch.einsum): 20 min learning einsum notation for tensor contractions and batch matmuls.
Finance: Operating Leverage — high-fixed-cost/low-marginal-cost (software) vs. linear human-labor businesses.

days.title: Day 2: Transformer Internals & Vocabulary Mastery
days.subtitle: From attention mechanisms to the full LLM training pipeline
days.label: Transformers

tasks.text: Read 'The Illustrated Transformer' by Jay Alammar (~35 min). Focus on the Decoder half. Track how 1 token embedding becomes Q, K, V vectors.
Watch 3B1B Ch. 5: 'But what is a GPT? Visual intro to Transformers' (27 min).
Watch 3B1B Ch. 6: 'Attention in transformers, visually explained' (26 min). Visualize Q×Kᵀ as a token similarity lookup table.
Study the 4-stage pipeline: Base Model (pre-training) → SFT (instruction tuning) → RLHF/DPO (alignment) → LoRA (adaptation).
Watch Karpathy's 'State of GPT' Microsoft Build talk — conceptual overview of the Pre-training → SFT → RLHF pipeline.
Understand LoRA math: frozen W₀ [4096×4096] + trainable A [4096×r] × B [r×4096]. Calculate compression ratio (r=8 → 0.39% params).
Study Open Weights vs. Open Source licensing: Llama (restricted) vs. Qwen/Mistral (Apache 2.0) vs. OLMo (true open source).
Solve Problem Set — Day 2: O(N²) context bomb, LoRA compression ratio, Accounting triage (P&L vs. Cash Flow).
Watch MIT 15.401 Ses 1: Introduction & Course Overview (~1hr 15min). Map Balance Sheet to cluster state.
Watch MIT 15.401 Ses 2: Present Value Relations I (~1hr 19min). Learn Time Value of Money and PV operator.
Map: Income Statement = request throughput, Balance Sheet = cluster state snapshot, Cash Flow = actual memory I/O.
GQA (Grouped-Query Attention) & MQA: How sharing K/V heads across Q heads slashes KV Cache VRAM by 75%.
RoPE (Rotary Position Embeddings): Encoding token order by rotating Q and K in complex 2D space. NTK-aware scaling / YaRN for 128k+ context.
MoE (Mixture of Experts): Mixtral/DeepSeek-V3 gating router activating 2 of 8 experts per token — giant intelligence at small inference cost.
Finance: CapEx vs. OpEx & GPU Depreciation — H100/B200 depreciation over 4–6 years on balance sheets.

days.title: Day 3: GPU Architecture, SIMD & Parallel Computing
days.subtitle: From your CPU's AVX-512 to NVIDIA CUDA cores and memory hierarchies
days.label: GPU/CUDA

blocks.title: Morning — CPU SIMD to GPU SIMT

tasks.text: Compare i5-1135G7 AVX-512 (16 FP32 per cycle) to GPU SIMT (thousands of CUDA cores, 32-thread Warps, Streaming Multiprocessors).
Read NVIDIA CUDA Refresher blog series. Study GPU hierarchy: HBM (VRAM) → L2 Cache → SRAM (Shared Memory / Registers).
Understand FlashAttention: keeping intermediate matrices in fast SRAM instead of slow HBM round-trips.
Study the Roofline Model: Arithmetic Intensity = FLOPS / Memory Bandwidth. RTX 3090 crossover: 142T / 936G ≈ 151 FLOPs/Byte.
Memorize the hardware cheat sheet numbers: DDR4 ~45 GB/s, 3090 936 GB/s, A100 2039 GB/s, H100 3350 GB/s.
Solve Problem Set — Day 3: AVX-512 FP32 vs INT8 throughput, The Wrapper Margin Trap (2.5% gross margin!).

blocks.title: Evening — Finance: SaaS & AI Unit Economics

tasks.text: Study CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost), LTV (Lifetime Value), Gross Margin, Payback Period.
Calculate why traditional SaaS has 80% gross margins while poorly optimized AI wrappers drop to 30% (GPU inference COGS).
OpenAI Triton Language: Write Vector Addition & Fused Softmax kernels in Python. Learn kernel fusion to eliminate HBM reads/writes.
NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys) & PyTorch Profiler: Read GPU execution flamegraphs. Spot 'GPU starvation'.
Finance: Jevons Paradox in Compute — why making inference 10x cheaper per token causes total GPU spending to increase.

days.title: Day 4: Local CPU Inference on Dell Latitude
days.subtitle: Hands-on with llama.cpp, quantization, and your i5-1135G7 / 32GB RAM
days.label: llama.cpp

tasks.text: Master the footprint formula: RAM(GB) ≈ Params(B) × Bytes_per_Param × 1.2. Calculate Q4_K_M sizes for 7B, 14B, 32B, 70B models.
Understand why CPU inference is memory-bandwidth bound (not compute-bound) at ~45 GB/s DDR4.
Calculate theoretical decode ceiling: 4.7GB model on 45 GB/s bus → ~9.5 tok/s max.
Clone and compile llama.cpp from source with AVX2/AVX-512 flags for Tiger Lake i5.
Run llama-bench: profile CPU thread scaling (-t 4 vs -t 8), RAM allocation, tokens/sec during Prefill vs. Decode.
Solve Problem Set — Day 4: Will 70B fit in 32GB? Sweet-spot model sizing for your RAM.
Read ProfitWell (Patrick Campbell) guide on Value-Based Pricing.
Learn cost-plus pricing (charging per token) vs. value-metric pricing (charging per resolved ticket / automated PR).
Intel Iris Xe GPU Offloading: Compile llama.cpp with -DGGML_VULKAN=ON or -DGGML_SYCL=ON, compare iGPU vs CPU.
Speculative Decoding in llama.cpp: Use a 0.5B draft model alongside 7B target model and measure speedup.
mmap & Linux Page Cache: Inspect how llama.cpp uses mmap(). Run vmtouch to verify model pages aren't swapped.
Finance: Price Discrimination & Tiering — Good / Better / Best enterprise tiers (Rate-limited API → VPC → Custom LoRA).

days.title: Day 5: Inference Engineering, vLLM & Vast.ai
days.subtitle: GPU inference serving, PagedAttention, and cloud GPU penny-pinching
days.label: vLLM

tasks.text: Read 'LLM Inference Unveiled' / Learn Inference book. Study Prefill (compute-bound, TTFT) vs. Decode (memory-bandwidth-bound, ITL).
Understand PagedAttention: non-contiguous KV Cache allocation like OS virtual memory paging.
Study Continuous Batching: loading weights once and multiplying against 32-128 user prompts simultaneously.
Why inference matters more than training

Load $5 into Vast.ai. Rent a Spot RTX 3090 (24GB) or RTX 4090 for ~$0.15–$0.30/hr.
or Google Collab Nvidia T4 gpu testing
Spin up the official vllm/vllm-openai Docker container serving a 7B/8B AWQ quantized model.
Inspect Continuous Batching & KV Cache usage via vLLM's /metrics Prometheus endpoint. Connect to Grafana if possible.
Tear down the Vast.ai instance immediately after to save cents!
Solve Problem Set — Day 5: The OOM Mystery (25 users × 8k context × 160KB), API vs. Self-Hosted crossover math.

blocks.title: Evening — Finance: Time Value of Money

tasks.text: Study NPV (Net Present Value), IRR (Internal Rate of Return), and Opportunity Cost.
Apply to engineering: build in-house vs. buy an API. Evaluate if a 2-month project yields positive ROI.
Disaggregated Prefill & Decode Serving: Split Prefill onto compute-dense nodes, stream KV Cache over RDMA/RoCEv2 to Decode nodes.
Guided Decoding / Structured Outputs: Outlines or XGrammar compile JSON Schema into FSMs masking invalid logits — 100% valid JSON.
Multi-GPU Interconnects: PCIe Gen4 (~32 GB/s) vs. NVLink (600–900 GB/s). Why Tensor Parallelism bottlenecks on consumer PCIe.
Finance: FinOps & Spot Instance Arbitrage — stateless checkpointing layers for Spot GPU SIGTERM failover.

days.title: Day 6: Vector DBs, Hybrid RAG & Agentic Loops
days.subtitle: Qdrant, HNSW, BM25 + dense hybrid search, and building a ReAct agent
days.label: RAG/Agents

tasks.text: Write a Python script to ingest 1,000 markdown docs using bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings.
Inspect HNSW index parameters (m, ef_construct). Understand it as a multi-layered skip-list graph.
Combine Dense Vector Search (cosine) with Sparse BM25 using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
Build a raw 50-line Python ReAct Agent loop (while True: prompt → LLM JSON tool call → execute tool → append stdout). No LangChain!
Solve Problem Set — Day 6: Why pure vector search fails for hex error codes, The Infinite Agent Loop (context overflow).

blocks.title: Evening — Finance: B2B Sales & Problem Discovery

tasks.text: Read 'The Mom Test' (Rob Fitzpatrick) summary. Learn to interview engineers/managers for budget-backed problems.
Binary & Scalar Quantization in Qdrant: Cut RAM 32x using 1-bit compression + XOR/POPCNT, rescore top 50 in full precision.
Model Context Protocol (MCP): Anthropic's universal USB-C for connecting LLMs to tools via JSON-RPC servers.
Sandboxing Agent Code: gVisor (runsc) / Firecracker microVMs to stop prompt injection from wiping your host.
Finance: Switching Costs & Data Moats — Why wrapper startups die; build defensibility via proprietary workflow data.

days.title: Day 7: Production MLOps, Vertex AI & Capstone
days.subtitle: CI/CD → CT, model observability, and your SRE Incident RCA Agent
days.label: MLOps

tasks.text: Map CI/CD to Continuous Training (CT) and Evaluation Pipelines. Study Vertex AI Model Garden & Endpoints.
Study LLM Observability: Tracing with Arize Phoenix or Langfuse. Automated evals with RAGAS (Context Precision, Faithfulness).
Study Made With ML (Goku Mohandas) — free MLOps course with GitHub Actions, Docker, Ray, experiment tracking.
Build an SRE Incident Root-Cause Analysis Agent: connect Qdrant DB + local llama.cpp (or Vast.ai vLLM) to process K8s crash logs.
Expose the agent via FastAPI with Prometheus metrics (/metrics endpoint).
Solve Problem Set — Day 7: Latency Budget Decomposition (2s SLA), The 1-Minute CFO Pitch ($60k savings).
Review SRE Incident Drills: Work through all 10 production AI debugging scenarios.
Draft a 1-page business model canvas for an AI/MLOps problem from your 4 years of SRE work.
Define: buyer persona, quantifiable ROI (e.g., reduce MTTR 30%, cut GPU waste 40%), and pricing tiers.
K8s GPU Sharing: MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) hardware-partitioning into 7 slices, CUDA MPS for process-level sharing.
Semantic Caching & LLM Gateways: Deploy LiteLLM as proxy in front of Vertex AI / OpenAI / vLLM with Redis caching.
Finance: Writing the 1-Page Executive ROI Memo — Situation → Complication → Resolution → Financial Impact structure.
